key_insight: Discrete Model-Based Diffusion performs training-free combinatorial optimization directly over discrete variables using diffusion-guided sampling.
engineering_relevance: The method targets fast multi-robot coalition formation and scheduling, with reported solution quality competitive with mixed-integer programming and reinforcement learning at lower computational cost.
method: Use denoising diffusion within sampling-based optimization over discrete variables.
Approximate categorical reverse transitions with Monte Carlo sampling.
Establish a finite-step lower bound on global-optimum discovery probability that approaches one as denoising steps increase.
evidence_signal: Experiments on generic integer programs and heterogeneous multi-robot allocation problems outperform sampling-based optimization baselines in nearly all tested settings.
watch_item: The asymptotic probability guarantee does not establish a practical runtime guarantee; Monte Carlo sampling and denoising budgets remain implementation concerns.
paper_title: Discrete Model-Based Diffusion for Combinatorial Optimization in Multi-Robot Task Allocation
